title: Why is the night sky dark?
screen:
WHY IS THE
NIGHT SKY
DARK?

lines.speaker: zib
lines.text: Bolt! Why is the night sky dark, if there are billions of stars?

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Great question. If the universe were endless, every line of sight would end on a star.

lines.speaker: zib
lines.text: So the whole sky should glow?

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Bright as the surface of a star. Everywhere.

lines.speaker: zib
lines.text: Okay, that is definitely not what I see.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Correct. Because the universe has an age. About thirteen point eight billion years.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: So light from the farthest stars hasn't had time to reach us yet.

lines.speaker: zib
lines.text: Wait. The dark parts are where the light is still on its way?

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Exactly. And expansion stretches the light that does arrive, making it fainter and redder.

lines.speaker: zib
lines.text: So when I look up, I'm looking into the past.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Always. The dark is a clue that the universe had a beginning.

lines.speaker: zib
lines.text: So the dark sky is basically the universe still loading.
